name: A labsheet
description: one person, one work session, one printable page — what to fetch and from where, what goes in each reaction, what to write on every tube, which controls and what each one proves, and the questions the lab wants answered when the work is done
phrases: what a LabSheet object looks like
how is a work session recorded

requires.note: the only constructor — createLabSheet, addSample, addSection, addSource, addNote, addOpenDecision, setRecipe, setMastermix, setDestination, setProgram, setCheckpoint, addBlock. It enforces what this schema states.

id.description: stable and machine-facing: session number, then the operations it holds. `s4-gel-zymo-goldengate`

title.description: what a person reads at the top of the page

operation.description: the operation, or the session's name where it holds several

tube.description: what the labels on this sheet are written on, which is what decides how long they may be. → TUBE

labelMax.description: derived from `tube`, carried for the renderer. Never declared independently.

columns.description: the samples table's columns, in order, declared UP FRONT. Every row is checked against them: a row with an undeclared key is how a column nobody chose reaches paper.

samples.description: one row per thing somebody labels. A transformation is one job and three plates, so one job may produce several rows. No two rows may share a label — a label is an exact key, and two tubes under one key are two tubes nobody can tell apart.

sources.description: what to fetch before starting. Four states and they are not interchangeable.

well.description: printed only when the box tracks wells

made.description: an earlier session of this plan produced it; there is no box to give

unlocated.description: nothing in the inventory says where it is. A gap in the document, not proof the tube is missing — so the sheet asks and the returned workbook updates it.

askWell.description: the box is named and does not track wells, so the box prints and the well is asked

askClone.description: the construct is known and the clone is not, because an analysis has not happened yet when this sheet is written

link.description: slugs another sheet recorded its box and well under, so a formula can point at them rather than asking twice

mastermix.description: the mastermix plan from makeMastermixPlan: whether one is worth it, which components are shared, the scaled totals, and why. The renderer draws this; it does not recompute it.

destination.description: where the finished tubes go — the *to gel* box. Never a thermocycler, a block or a deck position.

program.description: the thermocycler program. Not a machine and not a block id.

blocks.description: in page order: extra tables the operation contributes, headings, and protocol transclusions written `{module_id}`

notes.description: prose below the table — the things that are procedure rather than a column

open.description: decisions this compiler refused to make. Carried rather than defaulted, and gathered in one list at the end of a run, because a labsheet showing a hole is right and a person reading eleven sheets to find the holes is not.

warnings.description: things true of this sheet that somebody should know before printing it — a label too long for the cap it goes on, for instance. Not fatal: the name came from the construction file and that is the author's to choose.

submits.description: where this sheet's product goes when it leaves the building. `sanger` today, or absent.

checkpoint.description: a routing instruction a host institution attaches — C6 knows a sheet CAN carry one and the four fields it must have, and nothing about which steps deserve one. → setCheckpoint

protocol_values.description: what each transcluded protocol is rendered with. A module called with none returns a confident sentence about somebody else's experiment.

dilution.description: the dilution table, drawn by the renderer because it carries live formulas

notes:
WRITTEN 2026-09-13. The labsheet is the toolkit's central noun and had no schema, so nothing could say what shape it is without reading the constructor. `models/labsheet.js` already ENFORCES most of this in code — declared columns, label length by tube, no duplicate labels, no side-label on a sideless tube — and this record is what makes those rules findable and quotable.

ITS INSTANCES LIVE OUTSIDE THE STORE, ON PURPOSE. A labsheet is built in memory by `models/labsheet.js`, rendered to a workbook, and handed to a person; the packet is a build artefact that goes in /tmp or beside the experiment, not a record C11 keeps. What the schema is FOR is the contract between the three stages — `jobsToLabSheets` produces it, Cortex's `checkpoints.py` adds to it, and `labpacket-to-xlsx.py` draws whatever it is handed — so the seam is written down rather than being whatever the renderer happened to read last. Said here because Cortex's `tests/test_schema_orphans.py` asks every schema with no dependents to say why: deliberate and forgotten look identical, and a session that cannot tell them apart writes a second, weaker schema for a thing already described.
